::: {#exm-integer-difference}
#### Real numbers that differ by an integer

On the real numbers $\reals$,
let $x \sim y$ when $x - y$ is an integer (@def-integers).
For example, $3.25 \sim 0.25$, since $3.25 - 0.25 = 3$,
but $0.75 \not\sim 0.25$, since $0.75 - 0.25 = 0.5$.
The relation $\sim$ is an equivalence relation (@def-equivalence-relation).

**Reflexive.**
For every real number $x$, $x - x = 0$, which is an integer, so $x \sim x$.

**Symmetric.**
Suppose $x \sim y$, so $x - y = n$ for some integer $n$.
Then $y - x = -(x - y) = -n$, which is an integer, so $y \sim x$.

**Transitive.**
Suppose $x \sim y$ and $y \sim z$,
so $x - y = m$ and $y - z = n$ for some integers $m$ and $n$.
Then

$$
\ba
x - z
&= (x - y) + (y - z)
&& \text{(the } y \text{ terms cancel)}
\\
&= m + n,
&& \text{(} x - y = m \text{ and } y - z = n \text{)}
\ea
$$

which is an integer, so $x \sim z$.

:::
